function.name: search_google
function.description: Performs a search query on Google and returns a list of URLs that match the search criteria. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term to query on Google.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. The number must be a positive integer.

language.description: The language for the search results.

filter.description: A flag to filter explicit content in search results.

date_range.description: The date range for the search results in the format 'MM/DD/YYYY-MM/DD/YYYY'. If not specified, searches across all dates.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the most prominent vaccine manufacturers around the world, grouped by region and specialty.  (The list is not exhaustive—many smaller companies and academic‑industry collaborations also contribute to vaccine development.)

| Region / Country | Company | Notable Vaccines (COVID‑19 & others) | Notes |
|------------------|---------|--------------------------------------|-------|
| **United States** | **Pfizer‑BioNTech** | BNT162b2 (Comirnaty) – mRNA COVID‑19; Prevnar 23 (pneumococcal) | Joint venture; first mRNA COVID vaccine approved worldwide. |
| | **Moderna** | mRNA‑1273 (Spikevax) – mRNA COVID; mRNA‑LNP influenza platform | Rapid mRNA platform; expanding to other infectious diseases. |
| | **Johnson & Johnson (Janssen)** | Ad26.COV2.S – adenovirus‑vector COVID; Fluzone Quadrivalent | Single‑dose adenoviral vector; also makes influenza and other vaccines. |
| | **Novavax** | NVX-CoV2373 (Nuvaxovid) – protein‑subunit COVID; Hepatitis B | Protein subunit platform; strong adjuvant technology. |
| | **Merck & Co.** | Gardasil 9 (HPV); Keytruda (cancer immunotherapy) | Also produces influenza and other vaccines. |
| | **Sanofi Pasteur** | Fluzone, Menveo (meningococcal), Vaxzevria (AstraZeneca) | Global vaccine arm of Sanofi; broad portfolio. |
| | **Bristol‑Myers Squibb** | Shingrix (herpes zoster) | Strong focus on immunology and oncology. |
| **Europe** | **AstraZeneca** (UK/Sweden) | ChAdOx1 nCoV‑19 (Vaxzevria) – adenovirus‑vector COVID; Cervarix (HPV) | Large global reach; partnership with Oxford. |
| | **GlaxoSmithKline (GSK)** | Shingrix, Fluzone, Menveo | Strong in influenza, meningitis, and HPV. |
| | **Sanofi Pasteur** | See above | |
| | **Bayer** | Fluzone, Menveo | |
| | **Merck KGaA** (Germany) | MMR, Varicella, HPV | European Merck, distinct from US Merck. |
| **Asia** | **Sinovac Biotech** (China) | CoronaVac – inactivated COVID; various influenza vaccines | One of the largest inactivated vaccine producers. |
| | **Sinopharm** (China) | BBIBP‑CorV – inactivated COVID; various influenza & hepatitis B | State‑owned; widely used in China and many LMICs. |
| | **Bharat Biotech** (India) | Covaxin – inactivated COVID; various pediatric vaccines | Indigenous Indian vaccine; also partners with Oxford for Covishield. |
| | **COVAXIN (Bharat Biotech)** | See above | |
| | **Takeda Pharmaceutical** (Japan) | Rotarix, Shingrix, various influenza | Strong in enteric and vaccine development. |
| | **Shenzhen Kangtai** (China) | Various inactivated vaccines | Emerging manufacturer. |
| **Africa** | **Serum Institute of India** (India) | Covishield (AstraZeneca) – produced in India; various influenza & hepatitis B | World's largest vaccine manufacturer by volume. |
| | **GSK** | See above | Active in Africa through partnerships. |
| | **Novartis** | See above | Has African manufacturing sites. |
| **Australia** | **CSL Behring** | Various influenza, hepatitis B, and other vaccines | Major global player. |
| | **Sobi** | See above | Focus on rare diseases and vaccines. |

### How to Use This List
- **Research**: If you’re looking into a specific vaccine or platform, start with the company that has the most experience in that area (e.g., mRNA platforms → Pfizer/BioNTech, Moderna; adenovirus vectors → AstraZeneca, J&J).
- **Supply Chain**: For procurement or supply chain analysis, note that many of these companies have multiple manufacturing sites worldwide (e.g., Serum Institute in India, Sanofi in France, GSK in the UK).
- **Regulatory Status**: Check each company’s regulatory approvals in your jurisdiction (e.g., FDA, EMA, WHO prequalification).

### Quick Tips
- **mRNA**: Pfizer‑BioNTech, Moderna, and recently Novavax (protein subunit) are leaders.
- **Adenovirus‑Vector**: AstraZeneca (ChAdOx1), Johnson & Johnson (Ad26), and Sputnik V (Gamaleya) are key players.
- **Inactivated**: Sinovac, Sinopharm, Bharat Biotech, and Serum Institute produce large volumes of inactivated vaccines.
- **Protein Subunit**: Novavax and some emerging companies (e.g., Medigen in Taiwan) use this platform.

If you need deeper details on a particular manufacturer (e.g., production capacity, clinical trial data, or recent news), let me know and I can pull up the latest information.
